mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine typically costs between £1,900 and £3,600 for supply only, while a reconditioned unit ranges from £1,500 to £2,800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of AJ26 engine failure in a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold startup that lasts 1-2 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Given the typical market value of a 1999-2002 Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 (£1,500-£4,000), a full engine replacement often approaches the vehicle's total value.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to reprogram the ECU after replacing my Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine swaps do not require full ECU reprogramming if you fit an identical AJ26 engine code, though the PATS immobiliser may require pairing.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 typically takes 2 to 3 working days.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 launched in 1999, it served as the flagship naturally aspirated petrol option for the X200 generation, delivering smooth, effortless cruising and refined power before being replaced by the updated 4.2L unit in 2003.

milestones.description: AJ26 4.0L V8 introduced, delivering 280-290hp and establishing the X200's premium petrol credentials with a robust dual-overhead-cam design.
Production of the 4.0L variant ceased as Jaguar transitioned the flagship naturally aspirated role to the updated 4.2L AJ33 V8, featuring revised intake geometry and enhanced low-end torque.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.group: Main Bearing Wear & Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
problems.h4: Main Bearing Wear & Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 AJ26 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Extended oil service intervals and the original composite timing chain guides degrade under heat cycles, allowing chain slack. This can lead to oil pressure drops and main bearing wear, or in severe cases, timing jumps and valve contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing plastic guides, metal tensioner, and chains before catastrophic failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Adds 50,000-80,000 miles of reliable service if caught early with no fault codes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded metal tensioners, bench-tested long block, supply & fit.
repairOptions.longevity: Lifetime solution with 12-month warranty; resolves all internal wear simultaneously.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8?
items.answer: Given the typical market value of a 1999-2002 Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 (£1,500-£4,000), a full engine replacement often approaches the vehicle's total value.
keyPoints: It is only financially viable if the car has low mileage, solid bodywork, and holds significant sentimental or classic value.
For most owners, evaluating the scrap or part-exchange value is the most prudent first step.

items.question: Do I need to reprogram the ECU after replacing my Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine?
items.answer: Most Jaguar S-Type 4.0 V8 engine swaps do not require full ECU reprogramming if you fit an identical AJ26 engine code.
keyPoints: However, the PATS immobiliser system may require dealer-level diagnostic tools to pair the new engine's ECU with your car's existing security module.
Supply and fit specialists often handle this ECU pairing as part of the installation service.
